# Reference

Look-up material: every key of the configuration files, with type, unit, whether it is required, its default, the values it accepts and what it means. The pages are **generated** from the schema in [`tools/nxconfig/model.py`](../../tools/nxconfig/model.py) and checked in; a test fails as soon as schema and pages disagree. For how the levels fit together, read [architecture overview, section 3](../architecture/overview.md#3-the-three-configuration-levels) first.

The driver and service modules have a page of their own, see [Modules](#modules).

| Page | Level | File | Fields | Objects |

| [Derivative description](derivative.md) | Derivative | `mcudb/<family>/<derivative>.yaml`, `mcudb/<family>/<part>.pinmux.yaml` | 254 | 44 |

| [ECU description (rte.yaml)](rte.md) | Project | `projects/<project>/rte.yaml` | 39 | 8 |

## Modules

[Modules](modules.md) - the catalogue of the 15 modules in `libs/bsw` (device drivers, services, libraries) and the 6 in `libs/bsp` (contracts, MCU drivers), plus the 6 with a manifest in the ports (`platforms/<family>/port`, `ecu/platforms/<board>`): purpose, the `board.yaml` and `project.yaml` keys each one reads, host tests and the stated verification with its note. Generated from the module manifests (`module.yaml`), the module documentation and `tools/test/tests.yaml` by the same command and checked by the same `--check`. All 27 modules have a manifest, 1 of them parked (`module.yaml.pending`). Verification stated: `hardware` 13, `mock` 14; every module states it. What is still missing is listed in the section [Gaps](modules.md#gaps) and by `--gaps`.

## Console

[Console commands](console.md) - the 30 command groups (114 commands) the application can register on its text console: syntax, purpose, the build or module each one needs, which groups each project gets and which commands need a person at the board. Generated from the command registration and help texts in the C++ sources, the CMake conditions, the module manifests, the projects and the board READMEs by the same command and checked by the same `--check`.

## How to read the tables

Each object of a file has its own table; the heading is the YAML path of the object, `[]` stands for an entry of a list and `<key>` for a key of a map. Columns:

- **Field** - full YAML path of the key.
- **Type** - `integer`, `number`, `string`, `boolean`, `list of …`, `map of … to …`, or a link to the table of a nested object. A type written `one of …, selected by kind` means the key `kind` decides which table applies.
- **Unit** - from the schema's naming convention `<name>_<unit>` (`system_hz`, `deadtime_ns`, `shunt_uohm`, `t_nominal_ddegc` in 0.1 °C) or from an explicit unit in the schema. `none` marks a number that has no physical unit on purpose (counts, indices, identifiers, addresses, selector and register values); _missing_ marks a numeric field whose unit the schema does not state yet - a gap to be closed in the schema.
- **Required** - `yes` if the key must be present. Optional keys take the default when left out.
- **Default** - value that applies when the key is left out, written as YAML. `null` means *not set*; what that implies is in the description.
- **Allowed values** - enumerations and the limits the schema enforces (ranges, lengths, patterns). `item:`, `key:` and `value:` apply to the entries of a list or map.
- **Description** - from the schema: the description or comment of the field, otherwise the first sentence of its object type. _missing in schema_ marks a field the schema does not explain. Nothing is filled in by hand: a gap here is a gap in the schema, and it is closed there.

Two short forms: an object whose table equals an earlier one (`routines[].stop` next to `routines[].start`) points to it and keeps its anchor. An object of the power stage or motor control is marked **after R1**: it stays in the schema and is checked, but is not part of the first release, so its page entry lists only the keys.

Not in these tables: rules that span several keys or files - references between levels, resource conflicts, derivative limits. Those are checked by `tools/nxconfig` (`checks.py` and the model validators) and reported with file, line and YAML path.

## Regenerating

```sh
.venv/Scripts/python tools/docgen            # rewrite the pages from the schema, from libs/ and from the console sources
.venv/Scripts/python tools/docgen --check    # exit 1 and name the pages if they are stale
.venv/Scripts/python tools/docgen --gaps     # list schema fields without description or unit, module and console gaps
```

The output is deterministic (no time stamps, schema order), so the check never fails without a change.
